info.name: BuildHub API
info.description:
Routes reverse-engineered directly from the Controllers/ and DTOs/ folders. Seed data comes from DbSeeder (BuildHub/DataSeeder.cs).

## Running it as an automated test

1. Set "Seeding:ResetOnStartup": true in appsettings.Development.json and start the API, so the database is wiped and reseeded.
2. Run the whole collection in the Collection Runner (or `newman run`). The '00 - Setup (run first)' folder resolves every seeded row's real id into a collection variable, so nothing depends on identity values happening to start at 1.

## Why the deletes moved

Every destructive request used to point at a row other requests read - deleting the client user, the Ceramics category or the bathroom quote request took their children with them (cascade FKs) and left the rest of the run looking up rows that no longer existed. Each update/delete now targets either a row this run created ('Add Category' -> 'Delete Category', 'Add User' -> 'Delete User', and so on) or a dedicated throwaway seed row that nothing else references:

| Request | Target |
| --- | --- |
| Update Category Type | seeded 'QA Spare Category' |
| Delete Category | category created by 'Add Category' (fallback: 'QA Scrap Category') |
| Update User Email | seeded 'QA Email Update User' |
| Delete User | user created by 'Add User' (fallback: 'QA Delete Target User') |
| Update Quote Request Status | seeded [QA-STATUS-TARGET] request |
| Delete Quote Request | request created by 'Create Quote Request' (fallback: [QA-DELETE-TARGET]) |
| Update Invite Status | throwaway invite on [QA-STATUS-TARGET] |
| Delete Invite | invite created by 'Create Invite' (fallback: second throwaway invite) |
| Accept Quote | quote created by 'Submit Quote' (fallback: seeded qaAcceptQuoteId) |

## Known quirks in the current controllers, kept as-is

- category/GetById has no {id} route placeholder, so [FromRoute] int id can't bind (id is always 0 server-side) - it returns 204 No Content no matter what you pass.
- category/AddCategory binds CategoryInputDTOs via [FromQuery], so it takes query params, not a JSON body.
- user/UpdateUserEmail and user/DeleteUser take id as a plain query param.
- Milestone/milestone accepts a body but the handler just returns Ok() and ignores it.
- QuoteService.SubmitQuote dereferences request.Project without an Include, so 'Submit Quote' returns 500 until the repo eager-loads Project.
- There's no controller yet for EscrowTransaction, Project or Product.

item.description:
Reads the seeded rows back and writes their real ids into collection variables.

Run this folder first (the Collection Runner does it automatically, since it runs folders top to bottom). Every other request uses those variables, so a reseed that hands out different identity values can no longer produce 404s.

Quote, contract and milestone ids cannot be resolved this way - those controllers have no list endpoint - so they stay as literal seed-order values in the collection variables.

request.description:
[FromQuery] CategoryInputDTOs - fields are bound from the query string, not a JSON body.

The name gets a timestamp suffix so each run creates a distinct row, and the test script looks that row's id up (the controller only returns a string) and points 'Delete Category' at it. That keeps the delete repeatable without a reseed; if this request fails, the delete falls back to the throwaway 'QA Scrap Category' seed row.

var id = row.categoryId !== undefined ? row.categoryId : row.CategoryId;

request.description: Targets the seeded 'QA Spare Category'. No product, quote request or sub-category points at it, so flipping its type can't affect any other request.

Deletes the category created by 'Add Category' in this same run; falls back to the seeded 'QA Scrap Category' when run on its own.

It deliberately does NOT target Ceramics/Kitchens any more: Products and QuoteRequests cascade-delete with their category, and a parent category with sub-categories can't be deleted at all (the self-reference FK is restrict).

id has no [FromQuery]/[FromRoute] attribute and no route placeholder - ASP.NET Core infers it from the query string because the body is already claimed by the UserUpdateDTO.
